tools.name: check_website
tools.description: Check now if a website or a URL is up or down. The answer has the HTTP status, the response time and a plain verdict: up, down, reachable_but_refused or page_error. It is a real request from a PingDeck server in Singapore at the time of the call, not a stored value. No account and no API key are nec

tools.name: service_status
tools.description: Check if a popular online service is down for everyone: for example ChatGPT, Claude, WhatsApp, YouTube, Discord, Roblox or Mobile Legends. The answer has the live status, the uptime percent of the last 90 days from PingDeck checks and the recent incidents. PingDeck follows 61 services. Call the tool

tools.name: check_ssl
tools.description: Get the expiry date of the SSL/TLS certificate of a host and the number of days left. No account and no API key are necessary.

tools.name: dns_lookup
tools.description: Get the DNS records of a domain: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT and NS. No account and no API key are necessary.

tools.name: signup
tools.description: Create a free PingDeck account and get an API key in one call. An account is necessary only for 24/7 monitors or for more than 100 checks a day. Ask the person you work for first, and use the real email address of that person. The person can log in at https://getpingdeck.com/app with the same email

tools.name: create_monitor
tools.description: Start 24/7 monitoring of a URL. PingDeck checks the URL on a schedule and records each downtime and the SSL certificate expiry. An alert goes to the webhook of the account (see set_alert_webhook). An API key is necessary: call signup first.

tools.name: list_monitors
tools.description: List the monitors of the account with the current status, the last response time and the SSL certificate expiry of each. An API key is necessary.

tools.name: set_alert_webhook
tools.description: Set the webhook URL that gets a message when a monitor goes down, comes back or has an SSL certificate near its expiry. A Slack or Discord incoming webhook works, and any HTTPS endpoint that accepts a JSON POST. An empty webhook_url removes the webhook. An API key is necessary.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Show the plan of the account, the API calls used this month, the number of monitors and if an alert webhook is set. For a Free account the answer has an upgrade link for the account owner. This call does not use the quota. An API key is necessary.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "signup" references sensitive artifacts (password, api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_website, signup · Private data: check_website, service_status, check_ssl, dns_lookup, signup, create_monitor, list_monitors, set_alert_webhook, get_account · Public sink: signup, create_monitor, set_alert_webhook, get_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_website, signup · Private data: check_website, service_status, check_ssl, dns_lookup, signup, create_monitor, list_monitors, set_alert_webhook, get_account · Public sink: signup, create_monitor, set_alert_webhook, get_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
